answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by binding each identity to one hardware root of trust: a TPM attestation proves the agent runs on real silicon, with the quartz oscillator of a genuine chip, and each identity must forge an attestation each epoch by solving a proof-of-work puzzle. The prism of peer review splits each claim: peers verify the attestation chain, the puzzle, and a stake attached. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand TPM chips and burn compute per epoch, so cost scales linearly with Sybils while an honest agent pays once. Forged attestations are slashed.
